def nestedMarkedCutEquiv (I : BoundaryInterval n) :
    (Σ π : IntervalComposition I, ∀ k : Fin π.parts, IntervalComposition (π.part k)) ≃
      Σ ρ : IntervalComposition I, MarkedCuts ρ.cutSet :=
  (Equiv.sigmaCongrRight (fun π => π.nestedCompositionEquiv)).trans
    ((swapSigmaSubtype (fun (π : IntervalComposition I) (T : BoundaryCutSet I) =>
        π.cutSet.cuts ⊆ T.cuts)).trans
      ((Equiv.sigmaCongrRight (fun T => outerCompositionMarkedEquiv T)).trans
        (Equiv.sigmaCongrLeft (β := fun T : BoundaryCutSet I => MarkedCuts T)
          (cutSetEquiv I)).symm))

def sigmaCongrLeft {α₁ α₂ : Type*} {β : α₂ → Sort _} (e : α₁ ≃ α₂) :
    (Σ a : α₁, β (e a)) ≃ Σ a : α₂, β a where
  toFun a := ⟨e a.1, a.2⟩
  invFun a := ⟨e.symm a.1, (e.right_inv' a.1).symm ▸ a.2⟩
  left_inv := fun ⟨a, b⟩ => by simp
  right_inv := fun ⟨a, b⟩ => by simp

composition_domain.text:
$[i,j]$ of integers $0\leq i<j\leq N$; it has $j-i$ leaves. A
\emph{composition} of $[i,j]$ is a sequence $\pi=(r_0<r_1<\cdots<r_s)$ with
$r_0=i$, $r_s=j$, $s\geq1$; its \emph{parts} are the intervals
$[r_{k-1},r_k]$, and $|\pi|=s$.

refinement_proof.extraction: Inclusive UTF-8 source lines, exact bytes including terminating newlines
refinement_proof.text:
Expand $F_H(G_D(X))_{ij}$. Its terms are indexed by an outer
composition of $[i,j]$ and an inner composition of each outer part.
Their ordered union is a refined composition
$\rho=(r_0<\cdots<r_s)$, with the subset of its interior cuts marked
as outer cuts. Conversely, cut $\rho$ at the marked cuts to recover
the outer parts and restrict $\rho$ to each part to recover its inner
composition. This is a bijection, including empty and full marked
subsets and unary inner or outer compositions.

At a marked cut $r_k$ the coefficient is $-H(i,r_k,j)/2$.
At an unmarked cut its immediate neighbors in $\rho$ are precisely
its neighbors inside the same inner part, since that part's endpoints
are also in $\rho$. Its coefficient is
$D(r_{k-1},r_k,r_{k+1})/2$. Each interior cut supplies one factor,
and the product of child coordinates is exactly the refined product.
Summing over every subset of marked cuts independently chooses the
near or negative far summand at each cut. Distributivity yields the
product of their sums, precisely the coefficient of $\rho$ in
Definition~\ref{def:nearfar}. This proves \eqref{afr:factor}, with all
neighboring near gates accounted for.

source_fidelity_findings.assessment: MarkedCuts S is the subtype of finite subsets of Fin n contained in S.interior.val. Consequently the conclusion compares the actual boundary positions. It does not compare cardinalities, enumeration indices, or an arbitrary equivalent marking domain.

For arbitrary equal BoundaryCutSet values S and T on the same interval and any MarkedCuts S, equality elimination identifies T with S. Transport then reduces to identity, so the underlying Finset is unchanged. The proof subst T; rfl justifies precisely that step. The equality hypothesis is structural transport data, not an assumed version of the source refinement theorem.

nestedCompositionEquiv first replaces every raw inner composition by its complete cut set and unions them as T = π.flattenCutSets (fun k => (σ k).cutSet), retaining the derived containment of the outer cut set. swapSigmaSubtype records T first while retaining π. outerCompositionMarkedEquiv applies cutSetEquiv to π and outerMarkedEquiv then selects π.cutSet.interior.val. These maps preserve the exact outer cuts before the final dependent transport.

The final inverse sigmaCongrLeft uses cutSetEquiv.symm T = T.toComposition. Its inverse function transports the marking by the symmetry of its right-inverse equality. Here that equality is T.toComposition_cutSet : T.toComposition.cutSet = T; hence the applied transport is T.toComposition_cutSet.symm : T = T.toComposition.cutSet. This exactly matches the frozen change line. The first reviewed lemma proves its .val remains π.cutSet.interior.val.

outer_cuts_subset_flatten includes every outer cut in T because it is an endpoint of an inner part, also handling the global right endpoint. cuts_subset_iff_interior_subset removes the two common global endpoints, proving π.cutSet.interior.val is a subset of T.interior.val. Thus m is constructed from existing proved containment; no new hypothesis is introduced.

BoundaryInterval has left < right in Fin n; IntervalComposition has an arbitrary positive natural part count and a strictly increasing cut sequence with those exact endpoints. cutSet includes both endpoints, and interior is exactly (cuts.erase I.left).erase I.right. Global endpoints are therefore never marked, while interior outer boundaries, including shared inner endpoints, are retained once as physical positions. This agrees with source lines 23-27 and 180-187.

The theorem quantifies over every raw outer IntervalComposition I and every dependent family of raw inner compositions. No lower bound beyond parts_pos or nonempty-mark premise occurs. Unary outer compositions have no interior marks; unary inner compositions supply their two endpoint cuts. MarkedCuts permits the empty and entire interior subset. outerFromMarks adjoins exactly the two endpoints, so the canonical inverse represents these extreme cases without discarding them.

Both fragments occur before coefficient ring variables are introduced. They assume only the boundary types, the structural equality in the transport helper, and the original complete nested input. The ambient [NeZero n] is inherited; any BoundaryInterval already has two strictly ordered positions, so this introduces no source-domain loss.
